mainTopic: A nine-year-old יבם's ביאה and whether it counts like a מאמר, plus the story of רבי יוחנן and his student רבי אלעזר
overview: The amud has two משניות about a boy of nine years and one day who has relations with his יבמה. The first משנה rules that a second act, by his brother or with her צרה, disqualifies her. רבי שמעון disagrees, arguing that a nine-year-old's ביאה is either complete or worthless. The חכמים treat it like a מאמר, and the גמרא notes that this does not fit בן עזאי. The second משנה rules that if such a boy dies, his יבמה does only חליצה, and his ordinary wife is exempt. If he grew up and married another woman, she may do יבום. רבא learns from the first case that a woman tied by two יבמין cannot do יבום even with no צרה. רב and שמואל (with רבי יוחנן) argue whether a nine-year-old's ביאה is like a מאמר, and the גמרא explains the משנה as one side of a תנאים dispute about a decree because of the צרה. The amud ends with a story: רבי אלעזר taught רבי יוחנן's ruling without naming him, and others tried to calm רבי יוחנן. The גמרא then begins explaining why he cared so much, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two nine-year-old brothers with the same יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a nine-year-old has relations with his יבמה and then his nine-year-old brother does too, the second brother disqualifies her for the first. רבי שמעון disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A boy nine years and one day old had relations with his יבמה. Afterward his brother, also nine years and one day old, had relations with her. The second brother disqualifies her for the first. רבי שמעון says: he did not disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with its first case: two young brothers, one after the other, have relations with the same יבמה. The חכמים and רבי שמעון disagree about whether the second act matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A boy of nine years and one day is old enough for his ביאה to have some legal effect, but not the full effect of an adult's יבום. The חכמים say the second brother's act still does something: it ruins the first brother's hold on her. רבי שמעון says the second act does nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A boy nine years and one day old, the youngest age at which his ביאה has legal effect
His יבמה: his brother's widow, waiting for יבום or חליצה
Disqualifies, meaning he makes her forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: In the first case, 'פוסל על ידו' is about the brother: the second brother's act disqualifies her for the first brother. It does not mean the second brother now acquires her.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: MISHNA: A boy nine years and one day old
who had relations with his yevama,
and afterward his brother had relations with her,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: who is also nine years and one day old,
he disqualifies her for him.
phrases.notes: 'For him' means for the first brother: the second brother's act spoils the first brother's connection to her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: he did not disqualify her.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים say a second nine-year-old brother's ביאה disqualifies the יבמה for the first brother. רבי שמעון says it does not.

steps.title: One nine-year-old with the יבמה and then her co-wife
steps.stepSummary: If the same nine-year-old has relations with his יבמה and then with her צרה, he disqualifies her for himself. רבי שמעון again disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy nine years and one day old had relations with his יבמה, and afterward had relations with her co-wife. He disqualified her through himself. רבי שמעון says: he did not disqualify her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its second case. This time it is one boy and two women (the יבמה and her צרה), instead of two boys and one woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say his second act, with the צרה, also has an effect, so now both women are forbidden to him. רבי שמעון holds the second act does nothing here either.

keyTerms.meaning: Her צרה: her co-wife, another widow of the same dead brother
Through himself, by his own second act

phrases.english: A boy nine years and one day old
who had relations with his yevama,
and afterward had relations with her co-wife,
he disqualified her through himself.
phrases.notes: He blocked himself. Because of his own second act, both women are now forbidden to him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: he did not disqualify her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא עַל צָרָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case: one יבם with two יבמות, instead of two יבמין with one יבמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים say his second ביאה, with the צרה, disqualifies, so he is forbidden to both women. רבי שמעון says it does not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון explains his reasoning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי שמעון's argument: either the first act counts and the second is meaningless, or the first does not count and neither does the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It is taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון said to the חכמים: If the first act counts as a real ביאה, then the second act does not count. And if the first act does not count as a real ביאה, then the second act also does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון explains to the חכמים why the second act does nothing in either case of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון sets up an either/or. If the nine-year-old's first act is a full ביאה, it already finished the יבום, so a later act has nothing left to do. If it is not a real ביאה, then the second act, done by a boy of the same age, is no better. The חכמים answer by taking a middle position: a nine-year-old's ביאה works like a מאמר, which is partly effective, so a second one can still have an effect.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument shows the real issue behind the dispute. The question is whether a nine-year-old's ביאה is all-or-nothing, or whether it has an in-between strength like a מאמר.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Shimon said to the Rabbis:
If the first act of relations is a real act,
the second act is not a real act.
And if the first act is not a real act,
the second act is also not a real act.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי שמעון's position in both cases of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Either way, the second act has no effect, because a nine-year-old's ביאה is either complete or worthless.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow בן עזאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא observes that the משנה does not match בן עזאי. It begins quoting him: one מאמר can take effect after another when there are two יבמין and one יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like בן עזאי. For it is taught in a ברייתא: בן עזאי says: There is מאמר after מאמר in a case of two יבמין and one יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a comment about who the משנה follows, and starts quoting בן עזאי to show why he does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים treat a nine-year-old's ביאה like a מאמר. So the משנה's rulings amount to rules about one מאמר after another. בן עזאי agrees that this works when two brothers each make a מאמר with one woman, because each brother has his own tie to her. This matches the משנה's first case, so the problem must lie elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא (a sage of the משנה period)
A rabbinic levirate betrothal: the יבם betroths the יבמה with money or a document before יבום
A second מאמר after a first one, and whether it still takes effect
Brothers-in-law who are eligible to do יבום

steps.confusionAlert: בן עזאי is talking about מאמר, not ביאה. The link is that a nine-year-old's ביאה counts like a מאמר, so his rules apply to our משנה.

phrases.english: Our mishna is not in accordance with ben Azzai.
As it is taught in a baraita: Ben Azzai says:
There is levirate betrothal after levirate betrothal
in a case of two yevamin and one yevama.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּבֶן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the חכמים's view, that a nine-year-old's ביאה is like a מאמר, to identify which תנא the משנה does not follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן עזאי holds that a second מאמר takes effect when there are two יבמין and one יבמה.

steps.title: Where בן עזאי and the משנה split
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי continues: a second מאמר does not take effect when there are two יבמות and one יבם. This is exactly where the משנה's second case disagrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is no מאמר after מאמר in a case of two יבמות and one יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes בן עזאי's quote and shows exactly why the משנה cannot follow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one יבם, his first מאמר completes his tie to the household, so a second מאמר with the צרה does nothing. But the משנה's second case says a nine-year-old's second act, with the צרה, does disqualify. That means the משנה allows a second 'מאמר' even with one יבם, which goes against בן עזאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Widows waiting for יבום (plural of יבמה)

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים treat a nine-year-old's ביאה like a מאמר. בן עזאי allows a second מאמר only with two יבמין and one יבמה, not with one יבם and two יבמות. Since the משנה's second case (one boy with the צרה) does disqualify, the משנה does not follow בן עזאי.

phrases.english: But there is no levirate betrothal after levirate betrothal
in a case of two yevamot and one yavam.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַאֲמָר אַחַר מַאֲמָר בִּשְׁתֵּי יְבָמוֹת וְיָבָם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes בן עזאי's statement and shows the clash with the משנה's second case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's ruling, that one nine-year-old's second act with the צרה disqualifies, goes against בן עזאי, who holds there is no second מאמר with one יבם.

steps.title: A nine-year-old who had relations with his יבמה and died
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if a nine-year-old had relations with his יבמה and died, she does חליצה but not יבום. If he married a woman in the regular way and died, she is completely exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy nine years and one day old had relations with his יבמה and then died. She does חליצה and may not do יבום. If he married a woman and died, she is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with two simple cases about a nine-year-old boy who dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nine-year-old's relations work only partly, like a מאמר. So the יבמה is now tied both to her first husband's family and to this boy, which blocks יבום, and she does חליצה instead. A regular marriage by a minor does not take effect at all, so his wife is not tied to his brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: A boy nine years and one day old. His relations count in a limited way.
She performs חליצה, the release ceremony.
She enters into יבום, levirate marriage.
Exempt from both יבום and חליצה.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In the first, the boy's relations with his יבמה count partly, so she needs חליצה. In the second, his ordinary marriage counts for nothing, so she is free.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A boy nine years and one day old
who had relations with his yevama and died:
she performs chalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage.
If he married a woman and died:
she is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ וּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It continues the theme of a nine-year-old's weak act of יבום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a nine-year-old had relations with his יבמה and died, she does חליצה only. If he married a woman and died, she is exempt.

steps.title: He grew up and married another woman, then died
steps.stepSummary: The boy had relations with his יבמה as a minor, then grew up and married another woman, then died. If he never had relations with the first after growing up, the first does חליצה only, and the second may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A nine-year-old had relations with his יבמה. After he grew up, he married another woman and then died. If he never had relations with the first woman after growing up, the first does חליצה and not יבום. The second does either חליצה or יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a harder case with two women: one he took as a minor, and one he married as an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first woman's tie to him was made only while he was a minor, so it is still weak. She stays in the same position as in the last step and does חליצה only. The second woman was fully married to an adult, so she is a normal widow who can do either.

keyTerms.meaning: Knew. Here it means had relations with.
The first woman and the second woman.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא עַל יְבִמְתּוֹ,
phrases.english: A boy nine years and one day old who had relations with his yevama,
and after he grew up he married another woman, and died:

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא יָדַע אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מִשֶּׁהִגְדִּיל —
phrases.english: if he did not have relations with the first one after he grew up,
the first performs chalitza and does not enter into levirate marriage,
and the second either performs chalitza or enters into levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשֶּׁהִגְדִּיל נָשָׂא אִשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the first case by adding a second, fully married wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first woman does חליצה only. The second does חליצה or יבום.

steps.title: רבי שמעון treats both women as full wives
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that the surviving brother may do יבום with whichever woman he chooses and does חליצה with the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: he does יבום with whichever one he wants, and does חליצה with the second.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first case of the משנה about the two women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In earlier steps רבי שמעון held that a nine-year-old's act either fully counts or does not count at all, with no halfway status. Here he treats the first woman as a full wife just like the second. So the women are two wives of one dead brother: one gets יבום and the other gets חליצה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
he consummates levirate marriage with whichever one he wants,
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the surviving brother, not the boy who died.

phrases.english: and performs chalitza with the other one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מְיַיבֵּם לְאֵי זוֹ שֶׁיִּרְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's opposing view on the case in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both women count as full wives. The brother does יבום with one and חליצה with the other.

steps.title: A twenty-year-old without signs of puberty is treated the same
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that these rules apply both to a nine-year-old and to a twenty-year-old who has not grown two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies both to one who is nine years and one day old and to one who is twenty but has not grown two hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by stretching the rules to cover an older man who never showed signs of adulthood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Age alone does not make someone an adult in these laws. He also needs שתי שערות. A twenty-year-old without them still has a minor's status, so his relations are as weak as a nine-year-old's.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hairs, the physical sign of puberty.

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֶׁהוּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Both one who is nine years and one day old,
and one who is twenty years old
who has not grown two hairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד שֶׁהוּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד, וְאֶחָד שֶׁהוּא בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens all the משנה's cases to include an adult-aged man who lacks signs of puberty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A twenty-year-old without two hairs has the same status as a nine-year-old.

steps.title: רבא: the two-brothers rule is not only because of a צרה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that the rabbinic rule about a woman tied by two יבמין (חליצה only, no יבום) should not be limited to cases where there is a צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the Rabbis ruled that when a woman is tied by two יבמין, she does חליצה and not יבום. Do not say this applies only where there is a צרה, where there would be a reason to make a decree because of the צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רבא stating how wide a rabbinic rule is. In the next step he will prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the Rabbis banned יבום here only because a צרה is involved, so people would not come to do יבום with two co-wives from one house. רבא rejects that limit. The rule applies whenever a woman is tied by two brothers, with or without a צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The bond of two יבמין: a woman tied to the family through two different brothers.
A rival wife (co-wife of the same husband).
Do not say. It warns against a mistaken assumption.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rava said:
That which the Rabbis said,
that when there is a bond of two yevamin,
she performs chalitza but does not enter into levirate marriage,
do not say this is only where there is a rival wife,
where there is reason to make a decree because of the rival wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן זִיקַּת שְׁנֵי יְבָמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion by setting the scope of the rule behind the משנה's first case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'חליצה, not יבום' rule for זיקת שני יבמין applies even where there is no צרה.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's first case, which has no צרה
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his point from the משנה's first case. There is only one woman there, so no צרה, and still she does חליצה and not יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: For here there is no צרה, and still she does חליצה and does not do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings his proof from the very first line of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the יבמה was tied both to her first husband and to the nine-year-old, which is a case of זיקת שני יבמין. There is only one woman, so no צרה is involved. Since the משנה still forbids יבום, the rule cannot depend on a צרה.

keyTerms.meaning: For here. It points to a proof in the current text.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that a woman tied by two יבמין does חליצה but not יבום applies on its own, even with no צרה. רבא proves it from the משנה's first case.

phrases.english: For here there is no rival wife,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה's first case, where there is only one woman.

phrases.english: and still she performs chalitza,
and does not enter into levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא הָכָא לֵיכָּא צָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim in step 10 with evidence from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the two-brothers rule does not depend on a צרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's first case (step 6): one יבמה, no צרה, yet she does חליצה only.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling matches a known ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה's rule about a nine-year-old who married and died is the same rule taught in a ברייתא: the wives of a שוטה or a קטן are free from both חליצה and יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He married a woman and died.' We already learned this in a ברייתא: a שוטה and a קטן who married and died, their wives are free from חליצה and from יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and points out that a ברייתא already teaches the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nine-year-old boy's marriage does not count as a real marriage. So when he dies, his wife has no tie to his brothers at all. The ברייתא says the same about a שוטה and a קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned it (this rule is already taught)
A person who is mentally incompetent
A minor, a boy under the age of adulthood

phrases.english: He married a woman and died, etc.
We already learned this,
as the Rabbis taught:
An imbecile and a minor who married and died,
their wives are exempt
from halitza and from levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנֵינָא לְהָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to an earlier clause of the משנה to link it to a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife of a שוטה or a קטן who married and died is free from both חליצה and יבום, because their marriage does not count.

steps.title: Why not treat a nine-year-old's relations like an adult's betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the רבנן should treat the relations of a nine-year-old like the מאמר of an adult. Then the second wife would be pushed away from יבום, and she should not be allowed to do יבום as the משנה said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A nine-year-old... after he grew up...' But the רבנן should treat the relations of a nine-year-old like the מאמר of an adult. Then the צרה should be pushed away from יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that the second wife may do יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A nine-year-old's relations with his יבמה is not a full יבום, but it is not nothing either. If it counted like a מאמר, the first woman would have a tie to two brothers. Then, like in other such cases, her צרה (the second wife) should also not be allowed to do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic form of betrothal that a brother gives the יבמה before יבום
A co-wife, the other wife of the same husband

steps.confusionAlert: The 'צרה' here is the second woman, the one the boy married after he grew up. The challenge is not about the first woman; everyone agrees she does only חליצה.

phrases.english: A nine-year-old, etc.; after he grew up, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's case from step 7: he had relations with his יבמה as a minor, then grew up and married another woman.

phrases.english: But let them make the relations of a nine-year-old
like the levirate betrothal of an adult,
and the rival wife should be pushed away from levirate marriage!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַעֲשׂוּ בִּיאַת בֶּן תֵּשַׁע כְּמַאֲמָר בַּגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the משנה and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the second wife may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a nine-year-old's relations counted like an adult's מאמר, the first woman would be tied to two brothers. Then her צרה should be barred from יבום, against the משנה.

steps.title: רב: A nine-year-old's relations are not like an adult's betrothal
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the רבנן did not treat a nine-year-old's relations like an adult's מאמר, so the second wife is not pushed away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The רבנן did not make the relations of a nine-year-old like the מאמר of an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the challenge by rejecting the idea it was built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, the relations of a nine-year-old do not create the kind of tie that a מאמר creates. So the first woman is not tied to two brothers in that way, and her צרה may do יבום, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the רבנן) did not make it so

phrases.english: Rav said:
They did not make the relations of a nine-year-old
like the levirate betrothal of an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא עָשׂוּ בִּיאַת בֶּן תֵּשַׁע כְּמַאֲמָר בַּגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise of the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A nine-year-old's relations count like a מאמר, so the צרה should be barred from יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב, they do not count like a מאמר, so the משנה's ruling stands.

steps.title: שמואל and רבי יוחנן: They certainly did
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and says the רבנן did treat a nine-year-old's relations like an adult's מאמר. רבי יוחנן says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: They certainly did. And רבי יוחנן also said: They certainly did.
steps.whatsHappening: Two other אמוראים disagree with רב and accept the idea behind the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל and רבי יוחנן, a nine-year-old's relations do work like a מאמר. This means רב's simple answer to step 13 does not work for them. The challenge to the משנה now comes back according to their view.

keyTerms.meaning: They certainly did (literally, 'they did and they did')

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: They certainly did.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עָשׂוּ וְעָשׂוּ.
phrases.english: And so too Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They certainly did.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: עָשׂוּ וְעָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's answer in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nine-year-old's relations with his יבמה are treated like an adult's מאמר.

steps.title: Then the second wife should not do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל and רבי יוחנן: if the relations count like a מאמר, the משנה should not let the second wife do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let them make it so? (If it counts like a מאמר, why does the משנה allow the צרה to do יבום?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the challenge of step 13, now aimed at שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב escaped the challenge by saying it is not like a מאמר. שמואל and רבי יוחנן say it is, so the משנה's ruling that the second wife may do יבום seems to go against them.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them make it so (and if so, the rule should follow)

phrases.english: And let them make it so?
phrases.notes: He's asking: if it counts like a מאמר, the צרה should be pushed away from יבום, so why does the משנה allow it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַעֲשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view of step 15 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a nine-year-old's relations are like a מאמר, the משנה should bar the צרה from יבום. But it allows her.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is a מחלוקת between תנאים. The תנא of the 'four brothers' case holds that the רבנן made a decree because of the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a מחלוקת between תנאים. That תנא of the case of four brothers made a decree because of the צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the real question, whether to decree because of the צרה, is a מחלוקת between תנאים. It starts with the תנא who did decree, and step 19 gives our משנה's תנא, who did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The barring of the צרה is not automatic. It comes from a rabbinic decree made because of the צרה. The תנא of the four brothers holds that decree. As the next steps show, our משנה's תנא does not, so the משנה letting the צרה do יבום does not prove that a nine-year-old's relations fail to count like a מאמר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים
Four brothers — the name of an earlier case in this מסכת
He (the תנא) made a rabbinic decree

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tanna'im.
That tanna of the case of four brothers
phrases.notes: This points to an earlier case in this מסכת, on דף ל״א, about four brothers where one did a מאמר.

phrases.english: made a decree because of the rival wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the issue is a מחלוקת between תנאים, so our משנה does not have to fit everyone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since our משנה allows the צרה to do יבום, it seems to show that a nine-year-old's relations are not like a מאמר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנאים argue over whether there is a decree because of the צרה. The four-brothers תנא decreed. Our משנה's תנא did not decree, so it allows יבום even though the ביאה counts like a מאמר.

steps.title: That תנא spoke of an adult, but a minor is the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that although the תנא of the four brothers spoke about an adult, the same rule applies to a minor. He mentioned an adult only because that case was about an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught us about an adult, and the same is true for a minor. And the reason he said 'adult' is because he was dealing with an adult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: how do we know the four-brothers תנא would say the same about a nine-year-old?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four-brothers case was about an adult who did a מאמר. One might think the decree is only for an adult. The גמרא says the word 'adult' was used only because that case happened to be about an adult, and the decree applies to a minor too.

keyTerms.meaning: He is standing on, dealing with (a topic)

steps.whatToRemember: רב says a nine-year-old's relations are not like a מאמר, so our משנה is simple. שמואל and רבי יוחנן say they are like a מאמר. The four-brothers תנא, who also holds this, bars the צרה by decree, for a minor as well as an adult. Our משנה's תנא, in step 19, makes no decree.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the four-brothers תנא's decree would apply to our nine-year-old case too. So the only difference between him and our משנה is whether to decree because of the צרה, not whether the ביאה counts like a מאמר.

phrases.english: And he taught us about an adult,
and the same is true of a minor.
And the reason he said 'adult'
is because he was dealing with an adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּגָדוֹל, וְהוּא הַדִּין בְּקָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 17 by showing the four-brothers תנא applies to a minor too.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that a detail in the earlier case (an adult) is only there because of how the case happened, not as a limit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The four-brothers תנא spoke only about an adult, so he might not decree for a minor.
steps.terutzMaskana: He would decree for a minor as well; 'adult' was mentioned only because that case was about an adult.

steps.title: Our משנה's תנא holds the relations count and made no decree
steps.stepSummary: The תנא of our משנה holds that a nine-year-old's relations were treated like a מאמר, and he did not decree against יבום because of the צרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this תנא here holds that they did treat it like a מאמר, and he did not make a decree because of the צרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It explains the other side of the מחלוקת between the תנאים: the תנא of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the תנא of the 'four brothers' case held that the רבנן made a decree because of the צרה. Our משנה's תנא agrees that the relations count like a מאמר, but he made no such decree. That is why our משנה still allows the second wife to do יבום. Now שמואל and רבי יוחנן fit with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They treated it as (the רבנן made a nine-year-old's relations count like a מאמר)
The תנא of our משנה here

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the defense of שמואל and רבי יוחנן. Their view is not a contradiction of our משנה. It matches one side of a real argument between תנאים.

phrases.english: And this תנא of here
holds that they treated it as [a מאמר],
and he did not decree because of the צרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי תַּנָּא דְּהָכָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ עָשׂוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the תנאים split that was opened in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: מחלוקת תנאים: the challenge only works against one תנא, not the one of our משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the relations count like a מאמר, the second wife should be pushed away, so our משנה contradicts שמואל and רבי יוחנן
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה's תנא holds that the relations count but made no decree because of the צרה, so יבום is allowed

steps.title: Why our משנה mentions a minor
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה's rule holds for an adult too. It mentions a minor only because the case it was discussing was about a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught us this about a minor, and the same is true of an adult. He said 'minor' only because the case was about a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why our משנה speaks about a minor, even though the rule is not limited to minors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 18. There the 'four brothers' תנא spoke about an adult, but his rule also covers a minor. Here our תנא speaks about a minor, but his rule also covers an adult. So the two תנאים truly disagree on the same issue, and the detail of minor versus adult is not the real difference.
steps.whatToRemember: Two תנאים argue. One says the רבנן made a decree because of the צרה, so there is no יבום. The other, our משנה, says there was no decree, so יבום is allowed. Each mentions minor or adult only because of the case he was discussing.

phrases.english: And he taught us about a minor,
and the same is true of an adult.
And the reason he said 'a minor' —
is because he was dealing with a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּקָטָן, וְהוּא הַדִּין בְּגָדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording of our משנה, just as step 18 explained the wording of the 'four brothers' תנא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Wording explained by context: the case named is not a limit on the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe our משנה's rule applies only to a minor
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies to an adult too. 'Minor' is mentioned only because of the case at hand

steps.title: רבי אלעזר teaches without naming רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר taught this teaching in the בית המדרש without saying it came from רבי יוחנן, and רבי יוחנן became upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר went and said this teaching in the בית המדרש, but he did not say it in רבי יוחנן's name. רבי יוחנן heard and became upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now leaves the legal argument and begins a story about the teaching we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's ruling, that the relations count like a מאמר, was repeated by his student רבי אלעזר with no credit given. רבי יוחנן took this personally. The rest of the story follows from this moment.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר went
and said this teaching in the study hall,
but he did not say it in the name of רבי יוחנן.
רבי יוחנן heard and became upset.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֲמַר לִשְׁמַעְתָּא בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal discussion to a story about how רבי יוחנן's ruling was taught
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר taught רבי יוחנן's ruling without credit, and רבי יוחנן was upset

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי tell the Tiberias story
steps.stepSummary: Hoping to calm רבי יוחנן, רבי אמי and רבי אסי remind him of a time when two sages argued about a door bolt so angrily that a ספר תורה was torn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי went in to him. They said: Wasn't there an incident in the synagogue of Tiberias, about a bolt with a knob at its end? רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי argued about it until they tore a ספר תורה in their anger.
steps.whatsHappening: Two sages visit רבי יוחנן and tell him a story that shows how much damage anger can cause. The גמרא is setting up a question about the wording of their story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is meant as a gentle hint: an angry argument between sages once led to a ספר תורה being torn. The message is that רבי יוחנן should let go of his anger. In the story the two arguing sages are equals, and that detail matters at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: A bolt used to lock a door
A knob at the end of the bolt

steps.confusionAlert: The רבי אלעזר in this story is not the student we just met. He is an earlier sage who argued with רבי יוסי as an equal, which is exactly what bothers רבי יוחנן later.

phrases.aramaic: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי.
phrases.english: רבי אמי and רבי אסי went in to him.
They said to him:
Wasn't there such an incident
in the synagogue of Tiberias
about a bolt that has a knob at its end,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּחְלְקוּ בּוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: which רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי argued about,
until they tore a ספר תורה in their anger.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The response of רבי אמי and רבי אסי to רבי יוחנן's anger
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anger between sages once led to a ספר תורה being torn

steps.title: Could great sages really tear a ספר תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses the story to ask: could you really think these sages tore a ספר תורה on purpose?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They tore' — could that enter your mind?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the story to object to the wording 'they tore.' It is setting up a fix to the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the words say the sages tore the ספר תורה themselves. That is unthinkable for great sages, so the wording cannot be taken literally.

phrases.english: 'They tore' — could that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרְעוּ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges a word in the story just told
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'they tore a ספר תורה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great sages would never tear a ספר תורה on purpose

steps.title: Read it as 'a ספר תורה was torn'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording: the ספר תורה got torn as a result of their anger, not on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: a ספר תורה was torn through their anger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by changing how we read the words of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change is from 'they tore' to 'was torn.' The sages did not tear it on purpose. It tore during their heated argument. The lesson about anger stays the same.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
that a ספר תורה was torn through their anger.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא שֶׁנִּקְרַע סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה בַּחֲמָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sages tore the ספר תורה themselves
steps.terutzMaskana: The ספר תורה tore by accident because of their anger

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא's grim prediction
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא, who was there, predicted that this synagogue would become a place of עבודה זרה, and that is what happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן קיסמא was there and said: I will be surprised if this synagogue does not become a place of עבודה זרה. And so it happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a prediction that came true, showing how serious the incident was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The torn ספר תורה was a bad sign for the place itself. When the synagogue later became a place of עבודה זרה, it showed how harmful angry arguments can be. This is the point רבי אמי and רבי אסי wanted רבי יוחנן to take to heart.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה שָׁם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִיסְמָא,
phrases.english: And רבי יוסי בן קיסמא was there,
he said: I would be surprised

phrases.aramaic: אִם לֹא יִהְיֶה בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת זוֹ
phrases.english: if this synagogue does not become
a place of idol worship.
And so it happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיָה שָׁם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן קִיסְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story after the wording fix
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The anger led to a terrible result: the synagogue became a place of עבודה זרה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן becomes even angrier
steps.stepSummary: Instead of calming down, רבי יוחנן got angrier, because the story compared his student to his equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He became even more upset and said: Colleagues, too?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts to the story, and the attempt to calm him backfires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sages in the story were equals arguing with each other. By using that story, רבי אמי and רבי אסי seemed to treat רבי אלעזר as רבי יוחנן's colleague and not his student. That made רבי יוחנן feel even more slighted.

phrases.english: He became even more upset,
he said: Colleagues, too?!
phrases.notes: He means: now you are making my student into my equal as well?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אִיקְּפַד טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן's reaction to the story told by רבי אמי and רבי אסי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן objects that the story wrongly treats his student as his equal

steps.title: רבי יעקב בר אידי quotes a פסוק about משה and יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי comes to רבי יוחנן and quotes a פסוק saying that יהושע did everything exactly as משה commanded him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אידי went in to him and said: 'As ה׳ commanded משה His servant, so משה commanded יהושע, and so יהושע did. He left nothing out of all that ה׳ commanded משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new sage, רבי יעקב בר אידי, tries to calm רבי יוחנן. He starts by quoting a פסוק, which sets up the argument he is about to make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes a chain: ה׳ to משה, משה to יהושע. יהושע was the perfect student who passed on his rebbe's Torah exactly. This is meant to parallel רבי יוחנן and his student רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: He went in to him (came to visit him)
He did not leave out anything

phrases.aramaic: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi went in to him.
He said to him:
"As God commanded Moshe His servant,
so did Moshe command Yehoshua,
and so did Yehoshua do;
he did not leave out a thing

phrases.aramaic: מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּה ה׳ אֶת מֹשֶׁה״,
phrases.english: of all that God commanded Moshe."

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי אמי and רבי אסי's attempt made things worse, a new sage tries a different approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהושע faithfully passed on everything משה taught him.

steps.title: Did יהושע name משה every time he taught?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בר אידי asks a rhetorical question: did יהושע really say 'משה told me this' on every single thing he taught?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, on every single thing that יהושע said, would he tell them: 'This is what משה told me'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי asks a question whose obvious answer is 'no.' He is setting up his main point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says יהושע kept all of משה's teaching, yet nobody imagines he quoted משה on every line. So teaching without naming your rebbe does not mean you are failing him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so that...? (a question expecting 'no')
This is what he told me

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עַל כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁאָמַר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Now, on every matter that Yehoshua said,

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה אוֹמֵר לָהֶם: כָּךְ אָמַר לִי מֹשֶׁה?
phrases.english: would he say to them: 'This is what Moshe told me'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עַל כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁאָמַר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק just quoted to set up a comparison.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether יהושע attributed every teaching to משה. The question is rhetorical and the answer is clearly no.

steps.title: Everyone knows where the Torah came from
steps.stepSummary: יהושע taught without naming משה, but everyone knew it was משה's Torah. The same is true of רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, יהושע would sit and teach without naming a source, and everyone knew it was משה's Torah. So too, your student רבי אלעזר sits and teaches without naming a source, and everyone knows it is yours.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב בר אידי answers his own question and applies it to רבי אלעזר. This is the comparison that calms רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the rebbe still gets the credit even without being named, because everyone knows who the student learned from. This compares רבי יוחנן to משה, the rebbe, and not to an equal. That fixes exactly what bothered him in step 26.

keyTerms.meaning: Plainly, without saying whose teaching it is

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יעקב בר אידי succeeded because he compared רבי יוחנן to משה and רבי אלעזר to יהושע, rebbe and student, which is exactly the relationship רבי יוחנן wanted recognized.

phrases.english: Rather, Yehoshua would sit and teach without naming a source,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַכֹּל יוֹדְעִין שֶׁתּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה הִיא.
phrases.english: and everyone knew that it was the Torah of Moshe.
So too Rabbi Elazar, your student,
sits and teaches without naming a source,
and everyone knows that it is yours.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יְהוֹשֻׁעַ יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹרֵשׁ סְתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rhetorical question of step 28 and applies it to רבי אלעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Teaching a rebbe's Torah without naming him is fine, because everyone knows its source.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן praises בן אידי's approach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, now calm, asks רבי אמי and רבי אסי why they could not calm him the way בן אידי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Why don't you know how to calm me down like our friend בן אידי?
steps.whatsHappening: The story wraps up. רבי יוחנן is calmed and points out the difference between the two attempts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that the משה and יהושע comparison worked, while the earlier story of two equal sages did not. The way you comfort someone has to fit what is actually bothering him.

keyTerms.meaning: To calm someone down, to make peace with him

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן talking to רבי אמי and רבי אסי, who tried to calm him earlier.

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אִי אַתֶּם יוֹדְעִין לְפַיֵּיס
phrases.english: Why don't you know how to calm me
like our friend Ben Idi?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם מִפְּנֵי מָה אִי אַתֶּם יוֹדְעִין לְפַיֵּיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of רבי יעקב בר אידי's words: רבי יוחנן was calmed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן אידי's way of calming was the right one.

steps.title: Why was רבי יוחנן so upset?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן cared so much about being quoted by name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what is the reason he was so very upset?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the story to ask a question. It is setting up an explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting this angry over not being quoted might look like caring about personal honor. The גמרא wants to show there was a deeper, spiritual reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Was upset, was particular about it

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason
that he was so very upset?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי טַעְמָא קָפֵיד כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends, the גמרא asks about the reason behind רבי יוחנן's strong reaction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why being quoted by name mattered so much to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רב asks how a person can live in two worlds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with רב's teaching on the פסוק 'I will dwell in Your tent forever,' which literally says 'worlds.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What does the verse mean, 'I will dwell in Your tent forever,' literally 'worlds'? Is it possible for a person to live in two worlds?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question of step 31 by bringing a teaching of רב. רב first points out a puzzle in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עולמים is plural, so it sounds like 'worlds.' רב asks how one person could live in two worlds, and the answer will connect this to being quoted after death.

keyTerms.meaning: I will dwell, I will live

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"I will dwell in Your tent forever (literally: worlds)"?
Is it possible for a person
to live in two worlds?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to why רבי יוחנן was so upset.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer is built from רב's reading of 'worlds' in תהלים, which continues in the next step.

steps.title: David begins his request to God
steps.stepSummary: רב begins to explain the פסוק: דוד made a request of הקדוש ברוך הוא. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, דוד said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: רבונו של עולם, may it be Your will...
steps.whatsHappening: רב starts explaining what the 'two worlds' means through דוד's prayer. The sentence is cut off here and finishes in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the plain reading, living in two worlds at once, is rejected. Instead דוד is asking for something, and we will see what that is next.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Rather, David said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world, may it be Your will

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר דָּוִד לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts resolving רב's puzzle about 'two worlds.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's words are a prayer to ה׳; the content of the request continues afterward.
